lore_summary.en: The last Parthian king sees a new fire rising from Pars. He fights it — and the old age ends.
lore_summary.fa: اردوان، آخرین شاه اشکانی، اشتباه کرد که اردشیر پسر پاپک را در دربارش نگه داشت. اردشیر که فره ایزدی داشت گریخت، شورش کرد و در نبرد هرمزدگان اردوان را کشت. با مرگ اردوان، پانصد سال حکومت اشکانی پایان یافت و دوران ساسانی آغاز شد.

scenes.body_en: Ardavan was the last of the Ashkanian kings, and he made the mistake of keeping near him a young man whose ambitions were larger than his station. Ardeshir, son of Papak, had come from the province of Pars — a region that had once been the heartland of the Achaemenid empire and that still carried a certain pride in its bones. He served in Ardavan's court, learned its rhythms, and watched. Then he stopped watching and started moving.

The Shahnameh tells it with the clean logic of destiny. Ardeshir had the Farr — the divine radiance that marked a king in the old Iranian understanding. Ardavan, looking at the same young man, saw only a subordinate who had grown insolent. He ordered Ardeshir confined to the stables. Ardeshir fled instead, taking with him a slave woman named Gulnar who had chosen his future over her master's. The pursuit began. There is a ram in the story — a great white ram seen bounding toward Ardeshir as he fled, a sign that the Farr was moving from the old dynasty to the new.

What followed was years of open war. Ardeshir raised Pars against the Arsacid overlord, taking city after city, building alliances, and refusing every offer of settlement. He was not trying to negotiate a better position. He was ending a dynasty. Ardavan mustered his forces for a final campaign and met Ardeshir at the plain of Hormozdgan. The old king fought well. He was not a weak man or a foolish one. He simply had the wrong kind of Farr — the kind that had already moved on.

Ardavan died in the battle. The Ashkanian line, which had held Iran for nearly five centuries through Greek interruption and Roman pressure and everything else history had thrown at it, ended on that field. The Sasanian age began the same day. The chronicle marks the transition without ceremony — one king falls, another rises, and the world rearranges itself around the new center of gravity.

battle.intro_en: Ardavan saw the fire rising from Pars and fought it. He fought it and lost. To face this gate you must understand what it means to be the last king of a dynasty that held for four hundred years.
battle.intro_fa: اردوان آتشِ برخاسته از پارس را دید و با آن جنگید. جنگید و باخت. برای مواجهه با این دروازه باید بفهمی آخرین شاهِ دودمانی که چهارصد سال پایید بودن چه معنایی دارد.

battle.intro_tg: Ардавон оташи бархостаро аз Порс дид ва бо он ҷангид. Ҷангид ва бохт. Барои рӯбарӯ шудан бо ин дарвоза бояд бифаҳмӣ охирин шоҳи сулолае буданки чорсад сол поид чӣ маъно дорад.
